chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God be pleased with him) narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shamar, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The people are two: one who gives relief, and one from whom relief is sought. As for the one from whom relief is sought, it is the believer; when he dies, he is relieved of the world and its tribulations. And as for the one who gives relief, it is the disbeliever; when he dies, the trees, the animals, and many of the people are relieved from him.'

key_terms.أَرَّاحَ: The one who gives relief (to others)
key_terms.اسْتَرَّاحَ: The one from whom relief is sought (others are relieved by him)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the believer and the disbeliever regarding relief after death according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* employs a linguistic play on the roots 'r-w-h' (relief) and 's-t-r-h' (rest) to contrast the spiritual states of the believer and disbeliever. While the believer’s death signifies his own liberation from worldly trials (*istarrāh*), the disbeliever’s death serves as a relief for creation (*arrāh*), a concept deeply rooted in Shia exegesis regarding the societal burden of the unjust. This duality highlights the cosmic impact of individual faith, where the righteous elevate the world while the wicked impose a weight upon it.
